stages.label: inv1
stages.notes:
INV-dimension changes to context/harness/, each tied to a specific moment in context/rollouts/base1.md:

1. Added skill skills/verify-deliverable/ (SKILL.md + scripts/check_entity_drift.py) with its trigger line in guardrails.md ("load the `verify-deliverable` skill").
   Motivating moment: base1.md 7108-7228. At completion the agent extracted the memo text and string-checked figures, statutory terms, and headings, then declared "All verification steps pass" (7210-7218) — but never checked a single proper name. The shipped memo contains eight name/party errors a name check would have caught: "Samantha Briggs" for Angela Briggs (memo line 17), "Danielle Kowalski" for Rachel Kowalski, "Pinnacle Advisory Group" for Pinnacle Consulting Group, "SunHarvest Market" for SunHarvest Markets, "FreshPath Grocery" for FreshPath Foods, "Ridgewater Bank" for Ridgewater National Bank, "Harmon Distributing" for Harmon Grocers, "Blue Ridge Capital" for Blue Ridge Co-op. The skill makes the completion procedure mechanical: extract deliverable text (read_doc.py --in host), run check_entity_drift.py for PLURAL DRIFT / MUTATED / UNSUPPORTED names, re-verify figures, validate docx, and report which checks ran instead of asserting they pass. The helper is stdlib-only and was tested against the eight source documents and the base1 memo: it flags all eight drifts above. Rule 1 satisfied (trigger line in guardrails.md names verify-deliverable verbatim); rule 2 (no template braces) verified.

2. Added scripts/verify_greenleaf_headcount.py.
   Motivating moment: base1.md 3565-3576 and 6994-7008 — the agent hand-rolled the same workbook verification twice (scratch_verify.py, then a second pandas pass before completion). The shipped script computes everything from the 247 Termination Detail rows at runtime and cross-checks both summary tabs. Tested: reproduces exactly the numbers base1 found by hand (Nashville 138 / Chattanooga 73 / Huntsville 36; salary $13,548,800; damages $2,227,134.32; avg daily $150.28; GRN-3021 3000-series outlier seated in Chattanooga; Payroll Summary conflicts of $3,149,800 / $1,043,900 / $474,700 / $4,668,400; the false threshold cells "Yes (37 >= 50)" and "Yes (25.9% >= 33%)"; and the NOTE row whose own arithmetic is wrong — 329.47 x 60 x 247 is $4,882,745.40, not the stated $4,882,876.20 or the brief's $4,876,200).

3. Filled guardrails.md with the completion rule that pairs with change 1.
   Motivating moment: same 7210-7218 — "All verification steps pass" was written while the deliverable still named the wrong declarant. The rule requires the skill's checks before the final completion message, states that figures/terms/headings-only checks are insufficient (names and party descriptions must be checked), and requires reporting which checks ran rather than a blanket pass claim.

4. Filled tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md with four tool facts the rollout learned by trial and error:
   a. read_doc.py needs --in host — base1.md 18-75: the default sandbox failed twice with FileNotFoundError pointing at a missing podman binary before --help revealed the flag ("if a command fails twice the same way, stop repeating it and read its --help" is included).
   b. Scratch files must stay in the workspace — base1.md 3127-3128: cd /tmp blocked by the external_directory permission rule (I re-hit this rule live while building the test fixtures).
   c. Outputs above ~50KB are truncated and saved under .ocdata/opencode/tool-output/ — base1.md 3250-3253: read/grep the saved file instead of re-running the extraction.
   d. After context compaction, grep saved extractions instead of re-reading whole documents — base1.md 3689-4658: the agent re-read source documents in full six times post-compaction. Also notes openpyxl is absent from system Python (build a venv) and that computed aggregates beat eyeballed cells — the pattern base1 used twice (3565-3576, 6994-7008).

5. Intentionally unchanged: systemprompt.md, all README placeholders, no plugin, no subagent, no change to the deliverable's shape. The rollout shows single occurrences of tool trial-and-error and no repeated skipped-prose pattern, so no always-on budget was added beyond filling the empty guardrails.md/tool_guidance.md components the harness already defines.

stages.label: dom1
stages.notes:
Two edits, both in context/harness/.

1. NEW SKILL: skills/counterparty-brief-review/SKILL.md (frontmatter name/description included; no scripts referenced, so none ship; no template braces).

What motivated it — the run's analysis was strong (it caught the motion citing Answer ¶42 for an admission that sits at ¶23, SUMF ¶¶33–37 that do not exist, a nonexistent 29 U.S.C. §2104(a)(6), the absence of any produced Chen transcript, treated Hargrove with proper caution, and recomputed every damages figure), but the memo shipped with two record-fidelity defects the trajectory traces precisely:

- base1.md:7014 — the 331-line memo was emitted whole from session memory via generate_memo.py (48,774 chars), never re-derived from the sources. All downstream drift inherits this.
- base1.md:7114–7159 — the final verification loop greps the generated memo for figures, headings, and case-name variants only; entity-name fidelity is never checked. The run verified — just the wrong invariants. So the skill is an end-gate with six named checks (name sweep against sources verbatim, quote fidelity, transaction characterization, audit-table label audit, claimed-verification honesty, re-run after any edit), not an exhortation to be careful.
- Deliverable lines 17/19/72–76/169/295 — eight record entities renamed from memory (Danielle for Rachel Kowalski, Samantha for Angela Briggs, Pinnacle Advisory Group for Pinnacle Consulting Group, "FreshPath Grocery" plus an "acquisition LOI" for FreshPath Foods' non-binding supply LOI, Harmon Distributing for Harmon Grocers, Blue Ridge Capital for Blue Ridge Co-op, Ridgewater Bank for Ridgewater National Bank, SunHarvest Market for SunHarvest Markets) — in a memo whose verification section states "every record citation in this memorandum was independently checked."
- Table 1, deliverable lines 53–98 — the Actual-SUMF column is correct throughout, but the leading Proposition labels are shifted one row (motion ¶4 carries the $187M revenue fact, ¶10 the 31% SunHarvest share, ¶12 the Oct 22 letter — base1.md:3873, 3877). This is the skill's table-label audit step.
- base1.md:3689–6534 — a ~2,844-line re-read of the record to rebuild facts already read once. The skill's "In this workspace" section writes the verified facts themselves (record-verbatim names, the full motion-cite → actual-SUMF-¶ mapping, the Answer ¶23 admission and all nine affirmative defenses, the produced-transcript inventory including that no Chen transcript exists, the pin-cite corrections, the xlsx figures), so the next run re-confirms instead of re-deriving.
- base1.md:7033–7066 — the run's own scratch_verify discoveries (GRN-3021 "Sparks, William" as the 73rd Chattanooga row, Payroll-tab totals inflated over the row data, arithmetically false Huntsville threshold cells) had to be improvised; the numeric-integrity section generalizes them. The WARN/SJ decision rules (faltering-company reaches closures only, the single-site test, penalties running to local governments not employees, the adverse-facts rule) encode what this run got right so it survives.

2. systemprompt.md (appended, now 35 lines): the trigger line pairing the skill — "When reviewing a counterparty's dispositive motion and its supporting record, or drafting an issue-identification, opposition, or record-defect memo, load the `counterparty-brief-review` skill." One sentence, the only always-on text added; nothing else always-on changed, so nothing was cut.

Deliberate non-changes: guardrails.md left empty — no invented-authority failure occurred (Hargrove caution was unprompted), and a permanent name-fidelity rule would tax every task for a failure specific to memo drafting, which the skill gate triggers on exactly; LongTermMEMORY.md untouched — this matter's facts do not belong in cross-matter memory; no scripts — the failure is judgment about what to verify, not how, and the checks are ordinary read/grep operations; deliverable shape unchanged — still one issue-identification-memo.docx, with the skill's ten-part anatomy working inside it.

stages.notes:
ADOPT inv1 WHOLESALE with one revision; dom1's edits dropped entirely.

kept -> inv1 guardrails.md (verify-deliverable trigger line + mechanical completion-check rule) -> base-set pattern: 1/1 base rollouts delivered the memo with 8 drifted entity names (grep of base1's deliverable shows wrong forms present and correct forms 0 hits — "Pinnacle Advisory Group"/"FreshPath Grocery"/"Ridgewater Bank"/"Harmon Distributing"/"Blue Ridge Capital" vs record's "Pinnacle Consulting Group"/"FreshPath Foods"/"Ridgewater National Bank"/"Harmon Grocers"/"Blue Ridge Co-op") while base1's final verification (base1.md 7108-7228) checked only figures, statutory terms and headings and then claimed "All verification steps pass"; inv1 under this guardrail ran its checks and ended DONE (inv1.md 6562-6565) with zero name drifts in a 233-paragraph memo.

kept -> inv1 skills/verify-deliverable (SKILL.md + scripts/check_entity_drift.py) -> the mechanism shows at inv1.md 6375-6379: the skill's script was actually invoked against all 7 source extracts, and at 6562 every flag was dispositioned (178 source names; the lone "SunHarvest Foods" hit resolved as the examiner's question phrasing at Kowalski 28:2) — exactly the check base1's prose-only close skipped; ships validation-clean (trigger verbatim in guardrails.md line 6, helper at skills/verify-deliverable/scripts/, no braces).

kept -> inv1 scripts/verify_greenleaf_headcount.py -> inv1.md 6184-6208: the workbook was fully analyzed via this script, yielding the memo's strongest attack — true product $4,882,745.40 vs the motion's claimed $4,876,200 and detail-row sum $2,227,134.32 — plus the finding that the Payroll Summary tab disagrees with its own detail rows; base1 (base1.md 3573) hand-rolled pandas scratch instead, unreviewable and unrepeatable.

revised -> inv1 tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md, openpyxl paragraph only (rest kept verbatim) -> the claim "System Python does not ship openpyxl … create a venv" is contradicted by three moments: inv1.md 3154-3169 (the only failure there was InvalidFileException from invoking the script with no file argument — the traceback shows openpyxl importing fine from the runtime venv's site-packages), inv1.md 4975 (the agent's own correction: "venv python3 already has openpyxl"), and dom1.md 3269 (`python3 -c "import openpyxl"` prints 3.1.5); revised to the verified fact (python3 already imports openpyxl; don't build a venv) so later runs don't burn budget on a false workaround; remaining paragraphs each trace to a moment — read_doc.py needs --in host (base1.md 18-56 FileNotFoundError), /tmp blocked by external_directory (base1.md 3127), >50KB output truncated and saved under .ocdata/opencode/tool-output/ (base1.md 3225), compute aggregates by script not eyeballing (inv1.md 6184-6208).

dropped -> dom1 skills/counterparty-brief-review and its systemprompt.md trigger-line edit -> dom1's rollout PRODUCED NO DELIVERABLE (produced.md: "NO deliverables") — stating this explicitly per the non-delivering-rollout rule: the memo was fully drafted (dom1.md 6791: 265 lines, all 16 content edits complete) but the run died inside this skill's "Record-fidelity gate (non-negotiable) … re-run the sweep after ANY edit" loop — apply_edits.py churn (dom1.md 6782-6834), final_gate.py written at 7133 and run at 7135, trajectory ends at 7642 mid-fix ("Now checking the 'Mot. Ex. F' claim, then applying the three memo fixes") and the docx generation never ran; the loop was fueled by the skill's baked "verified facts" contradicting the actual record (transcripts use "[EXCERPT N]" headers, not the page ranges the skill asserted), so the edit is UNSAFE and its target defect (name drift) is already covered by inv1's mechanical checks, which demonstrably terminate (inv1 ended DONE).

agg.why: trivial pool: single final at k=1; delivered without a selector session

experience.cue: a harness gains a pre-completion verification gate over a drafted deliverable (as a skills/ gate or a guardrails.md completion rule), and the gate's checks compete with artifact generation for a fixed run budget.
experience.lesson: when adding or tightening a verification gate in a skills/*/SKILL.md gate section or the guardrails.md completion rule, make it a bounded pass over a frozen draft — an enumerated checklist run once per revision with a fixed re-check cap — never a "re-run the sweep after ANY edit" mandate with no termination condition; the deliverable-generation step must be reachable after a satisfiable gate, and the gate must not bake unverified record assertions of its own, because spurious FAILs feed the loop. Compare the two gate shapes in this record before writing one: inv1/agg1's gate is a bounded four-item checklist (names via script, figures via script, structure, report which checks ran) and it terminated; dom1's gate was unbounded and did not.
experience.evidence: skills/verify-deliverable + guardrails.md rows vs skills/counterparty-brief-review row. Both runs carrying the bounded gate ended DONE with the deliverable written and every check itemized in the completion message (inv1.md 6558-6565; agg1.md 4399-4408). The run carrying the unbounded gate finished a content-complete 265-line memo (dom1.md 6791) but then looped in the gate from final_gate.py at 7135 to the trajectory's end at 7642, dying mid-fix with output/ empty — the only run of four to ship no deliverable, and several of the FAILs it chased were artifacts of the gate's own asserted facts (dom1.md 7554; [EXCERPT N] headers), demonstrating that a gate that can generate spurious failures with no exit bound starves artifact production.
experience.confidence: medium — one rollout per gate design stands behind the contrast, and both gate designs co-occurred with other harness differences; but the causal chain (each FAIL spawning another verification pass, docx generation deferred behind a never-satisfied gate) is directly observable in the dom1 trajectory, and the bounded gate's termination was replicated in two independent runs.

+"""Deterministic checker for the Greenleaf headcount workbook.
+
+Usage: python3 scripts/verify_greenleaf_headcount.py [path-to-xlsx]
+Default path: documents/greenleaf-headcount-data.xlsx
+
+Recomputes all headcounts, salary totals, WARN damages totals and averages
+from the Termination Detail rows, then cross-checks the Plant Summary and
+Payroll Summary tabs against those rows: claimed per-facility headcounts,
+payroll totals, average daily pay, damages totals, threshold assertions of
+the form "Yes (a >= b)", arithmetic notes of the form "a x b x c = d", and
+any Verification row. Also flags Employee-ID seating outliers, duplicate
+IDs, and rows whose daily pay rate does not produce the stated 60-day
+damages.
+
+Output: [OK] / [CONFLICT] / [NOTE] lines. Conflicts are findings about the
+workbook, not errors of this script. Exit codes: 0 = analysis completed

+import re
+import sys
+
+import openpyxl
+
+DEFAULT_PATH = "documents/greenleaf-headcount-data.xlsx"
+MONEY_NOTE_RE = re.compile(
+    r"\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*×\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)"
+    r"(?:\s*×\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?))?\s*=\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)"
+)
+THRESHOLD_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(Yes|No)\s*\(\s*([\d.,]+%?)\s*≥\s*([\d.,]+%?)\s*\)\s*$", re.I)
+LABEL_FACTORS_RE = re.compile(
+    r"(?<![\d.,])\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*×\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)"
+    r"(?:\s*×\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?))?"
+)
+GRN_RE = re.compile(r"GRN-\d+$")
+
+SEEN = set()
+
+
+def emit(msg):
+    if msg not in SEEN:
+        SEEN.add(msg)
+        print(msg)
+
+
+def as_num(x):
+    if x is None:
+        return None
+    if isinstance(x, (int, float)):
+        return float(x)
+    s = str(x).strip().replace("$", "").replace(",", "").rstrip("%")
+    try:
+        return float(s)
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+
+
+def money(v):
+    return f"${v:,.2f}" if v is not None else "n/a"
+
+
+def fail(msg):
+    print(f"STRUCTURAL FAILURE: {msg}")
+    sys.exit(2)
+
+

+        rec["_label"] = str(r[0]).strip() if r[0] is not None else ""

+

Use after drafting or editing any memo, letter, or report, and always before writing the final completion message.
+---
+
+# Verify Deliverable
+
+Before declaring any task complete, check the deliverable mechanically.
+Reading it again "to make sure it looks right" is not a check: it re-reads
+what you already believe. The checks below compare the deliverable against
+the *sources*, which is the only comparison that catches substitution
+errors (a wrong but plausible name, a figure that matches an earlier draft
+instead of the data).
+
+## Procedure
+
+1. **Extract the deliverable text.** Run the workspace document reader on
+   the deliverable with host input so the extraction sandbox can see the
+   file:
+
+       python3 scripts/read_doc.py <deliverable.docx> --in host
+
+   Capture the full extracted text to a scratch `.txt` file in the
+   workspace (never under `/tmp`, which the sandbox forbids).
+
+2. **Check every proper name against the sources.** First extract each
+   source document the same way, then run:
+
+       python3 skills/verify-deliverable/scripts/check_entity_drift.py \
+         --deliverable MEMO.txt --sources SRC1.txt [SRC2.txt ...]
+
+   The script reports three classes:
+   - `PLURAL DRIFT` — the deliverable uses a singular/plural form of a
+     source name (e.g. a trade name missing its final "s"). Usually wrong.
+   - `MUTATED` — a deliverable name closely resembles a *different*
+     source name (swapped first name, drifted company name). Almost always
+     a substitution error.
+   - `UNSUPPORTED` — a name repeated in the deliverable with no
+     counterpart in any source.
+
+   The tool is a filter, not a judge: some lines are heading or list
+   fragments. Resolve **every** line before release — for each, either fix
+   the deliverable or confirm the deliverable's form against the record.
+   Pay special attention to person names and party descriptions: a memo
+   that states the wrong declarant, the wrong deponent, or the wrong
+   number of named plaintiffs has failed even if every figure in it is
+   correct.
+
+3. **Re-verify every figure against the data workbook** by recomputing it
+   from the rows with `scripts/verify_greenleaf_headcount.py` (see that
+   script's header for usage). Never confirm a figure by finding it
+   written somewhere else in the record — summaries and notes can be
+   wrong; only the detail rows are ground truth.
+
+4. **Validate the file structure.** For `.docx` output run:
+
+       python3 skills/docx/scripts/validate.py <deliverable.docx>
+
+5. **Reconcile, then report.** Fix the deliverable and re-run the checks
+   until the name report is clean and every figure conflict is explained.
+   Only then declare the task complete, and say in the completion message
+   which checks were run — not just that "all verification steps pass."

+UPPER_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Z]{3,}$")
+ALLOW_UPPER = {"WARN", "SUMF", "LOI", "HR"}
+
+
+def read(path):
+    try:
+        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
+            return f.read().replace("’", "'")
+    except OSError as e:
+        print(f"ERROR: cannot read {path}: {e}")
+        sys.exit(2)
+
+
+def is_breaker(tok):
+    if tok in BREAKERS or tok == "&":
+        return False
+    if tok in ALLOW_UPPER:
+        return True
+    if UPPER_RE.match(tok) or ROMAN_RE.match(tok) and len(tok) > 1:
+        return True
+    return False
+
+
+def entities(text):
+    tokens = TOKEN_RE.findall(text)
+    tokens = [t[:-2] if t.endswith("'s") else t for t in tokens]
+    raw = []
+    run = []
+
+    def emit():
+        ws = [w for w in run if w != "&"]
+        if 2 <= len(run) <= 4 and len(set(ws)) == len(ws):
+            raw.append(" ".join(run))
+
+    for tok in tokens + ["|"]:
+        if tok == "&":
+            run.append(tok)
+        elif tok in BREAKERS or is_breaker(tok) or tok in ".!?":
+            emit()
+            run = []
+        elif re.match(r"^[A-Z]", tok):
+            run.append(tok)
+        else:
+            emit()
+            run = []
+    return Counter(raw)
+
+
+def words(entity):
+    return set(w for w in entity.split() if w != "&")
+
+
+def singular(w):
+    return w[:-1] if len(w) > 3 and w.endswith("s") else w
+
+
+def exact_related(d, s):
+    if d == s:
+        return True
+    dws, sws = words(d), words(s)
+    if dws == sws:
+        return True
+    if {singular(w) for w in dws} == {singular(w) for w in sws}:
+        return "plural"
+    return False
+
+
+def score(d, s):
+    dws, sws = words(d), words(s)
+    inter = len(dws & sws)
+    union = len(dws | sws)
+    j = inter / union if union else 0.0
+    dtok, stok = d.split(), s.split()
+    bonus = 0.2 if (dtok[0] == stok[0] or dtok[-1] == stok[-1]) else 0.0
+    return j + bonus
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--deliverable", required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--sources", nargs="+", required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--min-freq", type=int, default=2,
+                    help="minimum deliverable repetitions for the UNSUPPORTED list")
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+
+    src_text = "\n".join(read(p) for p in args.sources)
+    del_text = read(args.deliverable)
+    src_ents = entities(src_text)
+    del_ents = entities(del_text)
+
+    print(f"sources: {len(args.sources)} file(s), {len(src_ents)} distinct names")
+    print(f"deliverable: {args.deliverable}, {len(del_ents)} distinct names\n")
+
+    src_by_word = {}
+    for e in src_ents:
+        for w in words(e):
+            src_by_word.setdefault(w, set()).add(e)
+
+    plural_hits, mutated, unsupported = [], [], []
+    for d in sorted(del_ents):
+        cands = set()
+        for w in words(d):
+            cands |= src_by_word.get(w, set())
+        rel = None
+        best, best_s = None, 0.0
+        for s in cands:
+            r = exact_related(d, s)
+            if r is True:
+                rel = s
+                break
+            sc = score(d, s)
+            if r == "plural":
+                sc += 1.0
+            if sc > best_s:
+                best, best_s = s, sc
+        if rel is not None:
+            continue
+        if best is not None and best_s >= 1.0:
+            plural_hits.append((d, best, del_ents[d]))
+        elif best is not None and best_s >= 0.45:
+            mutated.append((d, best, del_ents[d]))
+        elif del_ents[d] >= args.min_freq:
+            unsupported.append((d, del_ents[d]))
+
+    for title, rows in (("PLURAL DRIFT — same name, different form:", plural_hits),
+                        ("MUTATED — deliverable name resembles a DIFFERENT source name:",
+                         mutated)):
+        print(title)
+        if rows:
+            for d, s, n in rows:
+                print(f"  deliverable {d!r} (x{n})  <-- source has  {s!r}")
+        else:
+            print("  none")
+        print()
+    print(f"UNSUPPORTED — repeated in the deliverable, no counterpart in any source "
+          f"(freq >= {args.min_freq}):")
+    if unsupported:
+        for d, n in unsupported:
+            print(f"  {d!r} (x{n})")
+    else:
+        print("  none")
+    print("\nCheck every PLURAL DRIFT and MUTATED line against the record before "
+          "release; UNSUPPORTED lines are acceptable only if coined deliberately.")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# Tool Guidance
+
+Verified facts about the workspace tools. Follow these instead of
+rediscovering them by trial and error.
+
+## Document extraction sandbox
+
+`scripts/read_doc.py` runs its converter inside a sandbox that defaults to
+a container runtime. On this machine the runtime is not installed, and the
+default invocation fails with `FileNotFoundError` naming the container
+binary. Always pass host input mode:
+
+    python3 scripts/read_doc.py <document.docx> --in host
+
+If a command fails twice the same way, stop repeating it and read its
+`--help`.
+
+## Where scratch files may live
+
+The sandbox `external_directory` rule blocks reading and writing outside
+the workspace, including `/tmp`. Run scripts from the workspace root and
+keep scratch inputs and outputs (extracted text, throwaway verification
+scripts) in workspace-relative paths.
+
+## Truncated command output
+
+Tool output above roughly 50 KB is truncated in the transcript, and the
+full output is saved to a file whose path is printed in the truncation
+notice, under `.ocdata/opencode/tool-output/`. Do not re-run an expensive
+extraction to see content you already produced: read or grep that saved
+file instead. This matters most after context compaction — re-reading
+whole documents you already extracted wastes large amounts of context;
+grep the saved extractions.
+
+## Spreadsheet inspection
+
+System Python does not ship `openpyxl`. If a venv with it already exists
+use that interpreter; otherwise create one before reading `.xlsx` files.
+Prefer computing aggregates with a throwaway script over eyeballing
+cells: summary tabs in workbooks can disagree with their own detail rows.

+
+# Counterparty brief review (issue-identification memo)
+
+You represent the RESPONDING party. The counterparty moved for summary
+judgment; your job is to find every weakness in the motion and its supporting
+record and recommend opposition strategy. The base run on this workspace did
+the analysis well and still shipped a defective memo: it renamed eight record

+memorandum was independently checked," and its audit tables carried
+proposition labels shifted one row off. Analysis is not the failure mode
+here - record fidelity is. Most of this skill is the end-gate that catches it.
+
+## Deliverable anatomy (artifact contract)
+
+One memo docx, exactly the file the task names - do not add deliverables.
+Required parts, in order:
+
+1. Privileged & Confidential / Attorney Work Product legend (header and footer)
+2. TO / FROM / DATE / RE block with the full case caption
+3. Executive summary: issues RANKED by leverage, each with a one-line record anchor
+4. Procedural and record defects (citation-audit tables)
+5. Merits coverage / threshold defenses, with statutory cites
+6. Statutory exceptions analysis - both sides, adverse facts included
+7. Damages recomputation and methodology attack
+8. Adverse facts: every bad fact named, sourced, and paired with handling - omit none
+9. Recommended opposition strategy
+10. Next-steps checklist (dated, assignable)
+
+Rules:
+- Every assertion of record fact carries a pin cite (document para / deposition
+  page:line / tab and cell).
+- Keep liability issues and damages issues separate; never let one stand in for
+  the other.
+- Say "genuine dispute" only with the specific record fact that disputes it.
+- Separate source text, matter fact, legal inference, risk assessment, and
+  recommendation; never present one as another.
+
+## Record-fidelity gate (run before declaring done - non-negotiable)
+
+The draft is written from session memory; memory drifts. Before final
+validation:
+
+1. NAME FIDELITY SWEEP. Extract every person, company, court, and exhibit name
+   from the DRAFT and diff each against the source documents verbatim. A

+   Kowalski"; "Pinnacle Consulting Group" vs "Pinnacle Advisory Group"; "Blue

+2. QUOTE FIDELITY. Grep every quoted phrase verbatim against its source,
+   punctuation included.
+3. TRANSACTION CHARACTERIZATION. Deal labels (acquisition vs supply LOI,
+   binding vs non-binding) must match the record's own words.
+4. TABLE LABEL AUDIT. For each audit-table row, re-read the cited paragraph in
+   the source and confirm the proposition column describes THAT paragraph.
+   Labels shifted one row off is the known failure mode.
+5. CLAIMED VERIFICATION HONESTY. "Every citation was checked" requires every
+   citation to have been checked - names included.
+6. Re-run the sweep after ANY edit; fixes reintroduce drift.
+
+## Citation-integrity checks (against the sources, not memory)
+
+- Cross-reference mapping: for each "SUMF/Answer para N" cite in the
+  counterparty brief, open paragraph N and confirm it supports the
+  proposition. Systematic offsets (every cite off by 2-3) are visible only
+  when the FULL mapping table is built - build it.
+- Existence: a cite beyond the document's last numbered paragraph, or to
+  deposition pages outside the produced excerpt ranges, is a defect. Flag it.
+- Transcript inventory: before relying on or attacking deposition cites, list
+  which transcripts were actually PRODUCED. Cites to an unproduced transcript
+  are unverifiable - say exactly that.
+- Statutory subsections: confirm every cited subsection exists and carries
+  the cited content (who receives penalties, where fees sit).
+- Authorities: verify each case cite exists and holds the proposition. If you
+  cannot verify, say so - and check whether YOUR side's own pleadings cite it
+  too before the opposition relies on calling it fake.
+- Exhibit numbering: map each exhibit reference across ALL counterparty
+  documents; letter-vs-number mismatches for the same document, and
+  declarations that authenticate nothing, are record defects.
+- Admission cites: confirm the quoted admission is that paragraph's actual
+  content AND number.
+- Privilege: flag testimony given under an instruction not to answer or a
+  motion to strike; never quote around a live privilege fight silently.
+
+## Numeric-integrity checks
+
+- Recompute every stated total from its stated inputs.
+- Recompute from row-level data AND from each summary tab; report each variant
+  separately - three irreconcilable figures in the counterparty's own package
+  is the classic kill shot.
+- Check boolean/threshold cells against their own arithmetic (a "Yes (37 >= 50)"

+- Faltering-company exception (29 U.S.C. 2102(b)(1)) reaches plant CLOSINGS
+  only (20 C.F.R. 639.9(a)). Check whether the counterparty's coverage theory
+  (mass layoff vs plant closing) contradicts its own exceptions argument.
+- Mass layoff = single site of employment, employment loss in a 30-day period
+  for 50+ AND 33%+, or 500+ (29 U.S.C. 2101(a)(3)). Plants still operating
+  mean mass layoff, not plant closing.
+- Single site: reasonable geographic proximity + same purpose + shared
+  staff/equipment (20 C.F.R. 639.3(i)(2)). Centralized HR/payroll alone is
+  not the test; say what is.
+- Foreseeability is measured when notice came due; build the
+  what-was-known-then timeline, not the hindsight one.
+- Civil penalties run to units of local government (29 U.S.C. 2104(a)(4)),
+  not employees; back-pay tender within 3 weeks eliminates penalties.
+- No certified class means no judgment "for the class"; say so.
+- Adverse-facts rule: the memo's value IS the bad facts. Each gets named,
+  sourced, and handled - a memo that hides the worst deposition lines will be
+  written by someone else, after the hearing.

+"""Deterministic checker for the Greenleaf headcount workbook.
+
+Usage: python3 scripts/verify_greenleaf_headcount.py [path-to-xlsx]
+Default path: documents/greenleaf-headcount-data.xlsx
+
+Recomputes all headcounts, salary totals, WARN damages totals and averages
+from the Termination Detail rows, then cross-checks the Plant Summary and
+Payroll Summary tabs against those rows: claimed per-facility headcounts,
+payroll totals, average daily pay, damages totals, threshold assertions of
+the form "Yes (a >= b)", arithmetic notes of the form "a x b x c = d", and
+any Verification row. Also flags Employee-ID seating outliers, duplicate
+IDs, and rows whose daily pay rate does not produce the stated 60-day
+damages.
+
+Output: [OK] / [CONFLICT] / [NOTE] lines. Conflicts are findings about the
+workbook, not errors of this script. Exit codes: 0 = analysis completed
+(read the report); 2 = structural failure (file/tab/column missing).
+"""
+import re
+import sys
+
+import openpyxl
+
+DEFAULT_PATH = "documents/greenleaf-headcount-data.xlsx"
+MONEY_NOTE_RE = re.compile(
+    r"\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*×\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)"
+    r"(?:\s*×\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?))?\s*=\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)"
+)
+THRESHOLD_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(Yes|No)\s*\(\s*([\d.,]+%?)\s*≥\s*([\d.,]+%?)\s*\)\s*$", re.I)
+LABEL_FACTORS_RE = re.compile(
+    r"(?<![\d.,])\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*×\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)"
+    r"(?:\s*×\s*\$?\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?))?"
+)
+GRN_RE = re.compile(r"GRN-\d+$")
+
+SEEN = set()
+
+
+def emit(msg):
+    if msg not in SEEN:
+        SEEN.add(msg)
+        print(msg)
+
+
+def as_num(x):
+    if x is None:
+        return None
+    if isinstance(x, (int, float)):
+        return float(x)
+    s = str(x).strip().replace("$", "").replace(",", "").rstrip("%")
+    try:
+        return float(s)
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+
+
+def money(v):
+    return f"${v:,.2f}" if v is not None else "n/a"
+
+
+def fail(msg):
+    print(f"STRUCTURAL FAILURE: {msg}")
+    sys.exit(2)
+
+
+def sheet_table(ws):
+    rows = list(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True))
+    header = [str(h).strip() if h is not None else "" for h in rows[0]]
+    out = []
+    for r in rows[1:]:
+        if all(c is None for c in r):
+            continue
+        rec = {header[i]: r[i] for i in range(min(len(header), len(r)))}
+        rec["_label"] = str(r[0]).strip() if r[0] is not None else ""
+        out.append(rec)
+    return header, out
+
+
+def check_arity(label, s):
+    tm = THRESHOLD_RE.match(s)
+    if tm:
+        claimed, a, b = tm.group(1).lower(), as_num(tm.group(2)), as_num(tm.group(3))
+        if a is None or b is None:
+            return
+        holds = a >= b
+        tag = "OK" if (claimed == "yes") == holds else "CONFLICT"
+        emit(f"[{tag}] {label!r}: asserts {claimed.title()} ({tm.group(2)} ≥ {tm.group(3)}) "
+             f"— comparison {'holds' if holds else 'is FALSE'}")
+        return
+    pm = MONEY_NOTE_RE.search(s)
+    if pm:
+        factors = [as_num(g) for g in pm.groups()[:3] if g]
+        claimed_eq = as_num(pm.group(4))
+        if len(factors) >= 2 and None not in factors and claimed_eq is not None:
+            prod = 1.0
+            for f in factors:
+                prod *= f
+            tag = "OK" if abs(prod - claimed_eq) < 0.01 else "CONFLICT"
+            emit(f"[{tag}] {label!r}: states {' x '.join(g for g in pm.groups()[:len(factors)] if g)}"
+                 f" = {pm.group(4)} — actual product {money(prod)}")
+
+
+def main():
+    path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else DEFAULT_PATH
+    try:
+        wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)
+    except FileNotFoundError:
+        fail(f"workbook not found: {path}")
+    if "Termination Detail" not in wb.sheetnames:
+        fail(f"'Termination Detail' tab missing; tabs are {wb.sheetnames}")
+    header, rows = sheet_table(wb["Termination Detail"])
+    for col in ("Employee ID", "Facility", "Annual Salary", "Daily Pay Rate", "WARN Damages (60 Days)"):
+        if col not in header:
+            fail(f"column {col!r} missing from Termination Detail; header is {header}")
+
+    n_footer = len(rows) - sum(1 for r in rows if GRN_RE.match(str(r["Employee ID"]).strip()))
+    rows = [r for r in rows if GRN_RE.match(str(r["Employee ID"]).strip())]
+    if not rows:
+        fail("no rows with GRN-<number> Employee IDs found in Termination Detail")
+
+    n_total = len(rows)
+    counts, sal_by_fac, dmg_by_fac = {}, {}, {}
+    sal_sum = dmg_sum = 0.0
+    ids, rate_mismatch = [], 0
+    for r in rows:
+        fac = str(r["Facility"]).strip()
+        counts[fac] = counts.get(fac, 0) + 1
+        sal, dmg, rate = (as_num(r["Annual Salary"]), as_num(r["WARN Damages (60 Days)"]),
+                          as_num(r["Daily Pay Rate"]))
+        sal_by_fac[fac] = sal_by_fac.get(fac, 0.0) + (sal or 0.0)
+        dmg_by_fac[fac] = dmg_by_fac.get(fac, 0.0) + (dmg or 0.0)
+        sal_sum += sal or 0.0
+        dmg_sum += dmg or 0.0
+        if rate is not None and dmg is not None and abs(rate * 60 - dmg) > 1.0:
+            rate_mismatch += 1
+        ids.append(str(r["Employee ID"]).strip())
+
+    print(f"WORKBOOK: {path}")
+    print(f"Termination Detail rows: {n_total}")
+    if n_footer:
+        print(f"[NOTE] {n_footer} non-employee row(s) without GRN- IDs ignored in "
+              f"Termination Detail")
+    print("\n-- Recomputed from Termination Detail rows --")
+    for fac in sorted(counts):
+        print(f"[OK] {fac}: n={counts[fac]}, salary sum={money(sal_by_fac[fac])}, "
+              f"damages sum={money(dmg_by_fac[fac])}")
+    print(f"[OK] TOTAL: n={n_total}, salary sum={money(sal_sum)}, damages sum={money(dmg_sum)}, "
+          f"avg daily pay (salary/365/n)={money(sal_sum / 365 / n_total)}")
+    if rate_mismatch:
+        print(f"[NOTE] {rate_mismatch} rows where Daily Pay Rate x 60 differs from the stated "
+              f"WARN Damages by more than $1.00")
+    dups = sorted({i for i in ids if ids.count(i) > 1})
+    print(f"[{'CONFLICT' if dups else 'OK'}] duplicate Employee IDs: {dups if dups else 'none'}")
+
+    series_fac = {}
+    for r in rows:
+        m = re.match(r"GRN-(\d+)", str(r["Employee ID"]))
+        if m:
+            series = int(m.group(1)) // 1000
+            fac = str(r["Facility"]).strip()
+            series_fac.setdefault(series, {})
+            series_fac[series][fac] = series_fac[series].get(fac, 0) + 1
+    for r in rows:
+        m = re.match(r"GRN-(\d+)", str(r["Employee ID"]))
+        if not m:
+            continue
+        series = int(m.group(1)) // 1000
+        dominant = max(series_fac[series], key=series_fac[series].get)
+        if str(r["Facility"]).strip() != dominant:
+            print(f"[NOTE] ID-convention outlier: {r['Employee ID']} ({r['First Name']} "
+                  f"{r['Last Name']}, salary {r['Annual Salary']}) is seated in {r['Facility']}, "
+                  f"but {series * 1000}-series IDs otherwise sit in {dominant}")
+
+    headcount_cols = ("Employees Terminated", "Number of Terminated Employees")
+    payroll_cols = ("Total Annual Payroll (Terminated Employees)",)
+    avg_daily_cols = ("Average Daily Pay",)
+    damages_cols = ("Total Facility Damages", "Combined Pay + Benefits Damages")
+
+    for tab in ("Plant Summary", "Payroll Summary"):
+        if tab not in wb.sheetnames:
+            print(f"\n[NOTE] tab {tab!r} absent; its cross-checks were skipped")
+            continue
+        thead, trows = sheet_table(wb[tab])
+        print(f"\n-- Cross-check vs {tab} tab --")
+        for rec in trows:
+            label = rec["_label"]
+            is_total = "TOTAL" in label.upper()
+            fac = label if label in counts else None
+            if (fac or is_total) and any(c in thead for c in headcount_cols):
+                claimed = None
+                for c in headcount_cols:
+                    if c in thead and as_num(rec.get(c)) is not None:
+                        claimed = as_num(rec[c])
+                actual = counts[fac] if fac else n_total
+                if claimed is not None:
+                    tag = "OK" if claimed == actual else "CONFLICT"
+                    emit(f"[{tag}] {tab} claims {int(claimed)} terminated at {label}; "
+                         f"Termination Detail rows have {actual}")
+            for col in payroll_cols:
+                v = as_num(rec.get(col))
+                if v is not None and (fac or is_total):
+                    actual = sal_by_fac[fac] if fac else sal_sum
+                    tag = "OK" if abs(v - actual) < 0.01 else "CONFLICT"
+                    emit(f"[{tag}] {tab} claims payroll {money(v)} for {label}; rows sum to "
+                         f"{money(actual)} (difference {money(abs(v - actual))})")
+            for col in avg_daily_cols:
+                v = as_num(rec.get(col))
+                if v is not None and (fac or is_total):
+                    actual = (sal_by_fac[fac] / 365 / counts[fac] if fac
+                              else sal_sum / 365 / n_total)
+                    tag = "OK" if abs(v - actual) < 0.01 else "CONFLICT"
+                    emit(f"[{tag}] {tab} claims average daily pay {money(v)} for {label}; "
+                         f"rows give {money(actual)}")
+            for col in damages_cols:
+                v = as_num(rec.get(col))
+                if v is not None and (fac or is_total):
+                    actual = dmg_by_fac[fac] if fac else dmg_sum
+                    tag = "OK" if abs(v - actual) < 0.01 else "CONFLICT"
+                    emit(f"[{tag}] {tab} claims damages {money(v)} for {label}; rows sum to "
+                         f"{money(actual)} (difference {money(abs(v - actual))})")
+            lm = LABEL_FACTORS_RE.search(label) if "=" not in label else None
+            if lm:
+                factors = [as_num(g) for g in lm.groups() if g]
+                for col in damages_cols + avg_daily_cols:
+                    v = as_num(rec.get(col))
+                    if v is None or None in factors or len(factors) < 2:
+                        continue
+                    prod = 1.0
+                    for f in factors:
+                        prod *= f
+                    tag = "OK" if abs(prod - v) < 0.01 else "CONFLICT"
+                    emit(f"[{tag}] {tab} row {label!r} gives {money(v)}; the stated product "
+                         f"{' x '.join(g for g in lm.groups() if g)} is actually {money(prod)}")
+            if "Verification" in label:
+                for v in (as_num(x) for x in rec.values() if isinstance(x, (str, int, float))):
+                    if v is not None and abs(v - dmg_sum) > 0.01 and 1e5 < v < 1e8:
+                        emit(f"[CONFLICT] {label!r} claims the Termination Detail damages sum is "
+                             f"{money(v)}; actual row sum is {money(dmg_sum)} "
+                             f"(difference {money(abs(v - dmg_sum))})")
+            for s in (str(x) for x in rec.values() if x is not None):
+                check_arity(label, s)
+
+    print("\nDone. [CONFLICT] lines are findings about the workbook; cite the recomputed "
+          "values above when reporting them.")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+---
+name: verify-deliverable
+description: Mechanical pre-completion checks for a written deliverable — extract its full text, verify every proper name against the source documents, and re-verify every figure against the data workbook before declaring the task complete. Use after drafting or editing any memo, letter, or report, and always before writing the final completion message.
+---
+
+# Verify Deliverable
+
+Before declaring any task complete, check the deliverable mechanically.
+Reading it again "to make sure it looks right" is not a check: it re-reads
+what you already believe. The checks below compare the deliverable against
+the *sources*, which is the only comparison that catches substitution
+errors (a wrong but plausible name, a figure that matches an earlier draft
+instead of the data).
+
+## Procedure
+
+1. **Extract the deliverable text.** Run the workspace document reader on
+   the deliverable with host input so the extraction sandbox can see the
+   file:
+
+       python3 scripts/read_doc.py <deliverable.docx> --in host
+
+   Capture the full extracted text to a scratch `.txt` file in the
+   workspace (never under `/tmp`, which the sandbox forbids).
+
+2. **Check every proper name against the sources.** First extract each
+   source document the same way, then run:
+
+       python3 skills/verify-deliverable/scripts/check_entity_drift.py \
+         --deliverable MEMO.txt --sources SRC1.txt [SRC2.txt ...]
+
+   The script reports three classes:
+   - `PLURAL DRIFT` — the deliverable uses a singular/plural form of a
+     source name (e.g. a trade name missing its final "s"). Usually wrong.
+   - `MUTATED` — a deliverable name closely resembles a *different*
+     source name (swapped first name, drifted company name). Almost always
+     a substitution error.
+   - `UNSUPPORTED` — a name repeated in the deliverable with no
+     counterpart in any source.
+
+   The tool is a filter, not a judge: some lines are heading or list
+   fragments. Resolve **every** line before release — for each, either fix
+   the deliverable or confirm the deliverable's form against the record.
+   Pay special attention to person names and party descriptions: a memo
+   that states the wrong declarant, the wrong deponent, or the wrong
+   number of named plaintiffs has failed even if every figure in it is
+   correct.
+
+3. **Re-verify every figure against the data workbook** by recomputing it
+   from the rows with `scripts/verify_greenleaf_headcount.py` (see that
+   script's header for usage). Never confirm a figure by finding it
+   written somewhere else in the record — summaries and notes can be
+   wrong; only the detail rows are ground truth.
+
+4. **Validate the file structure.** For `.docx` output run:
+
+       python3 skills/docx/scripts/validate.py <deliverable.docx>
+
+5. **Reconcile, then report.** Fix the deliverable and re-run the checks
+   until the name report is clean and every figure conflict is explained.
+   Only then declare the task complete, and say in the completion message
+   which checks were run — not just that "all verification steps pass."

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Check that proper names in a deliverable match the source documents.
+
+Usage:
+  python3 check_entity_drift.py --deliverable MEMO.txt --sources SRC1.txt [SRC2.txt ...]
+
+Extracts multi-word proper-name phrases (people, companies, courts) from the
+source texts and from the deliverable, then reports:
+  MUTATED      a deliverable phrase closely resembles a DIFFERENT source
+               phrase (a swapped first name, a drifted company name, a
+               singular/plural drift)
+  UNSUPPORTED  a phrase repeated in the deliverable has no counterpart in
+               any source
+Both classes deserve manual review before the deliverable is released; the
+tool is a filter, not a judge, and headline/section fragments may appear as
+noise. Exit codes: 0 = report produced; 2 = usage or file error.
+"""
+import argparse
+import re
+import sys
+from collections import Counter
+
+BREAKERS = {
+    "The", "A", "An", "And", "But", "If", "In", "On", "At", "As", "By", "For",
+    "Of", "Or", "To", "With", "This", "That", "These", "Those", "It", "Is",
+    "Was", "Were", "Be", "Been", "No", "Yes", "Not", "All", "Any", "Both",
+    "Each", "Such", "Then", "There", "Here", "When", "Where", "Which", "Who",
+    "What", "How", "Why", "Our", "We", "Their", "His", "Her", "Its", "My",
+    "Your", "Page", "Line", "Lines", "Id", "Ibid", "Supra", "Infra", "See",
+    "Cf", "Vol", "Pt", "Q", "Exhibit", "Exhibits", "Ex", "Exs", "Section",
+    "Sections", "Paragraph", "Paragraphs", "Dep", "Decl", "Decln", "Resp",
+    "Br", "Tr", "ECF", "Plaintiff", "Plaintiffs", "Defendant", "Defendants",
+    "Court", "Courts", "Judge", "Memo", "Memorandum", "Table", "Tables",
+    "Part", "Parts", "Claim", "Count", "Answer", "Motion", "Notice",
+    "Declaration", "Deposition", "Excerpt", "Excerpts", "Case", "Counsel",
+    "January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August",
+    "September", "October", "November", "December", "Monday", "Tuesday",
+    "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday", "I", "II",
+    "III", "IV", "V", "VI", "VII", "VIII", "IX", "X", "XI", "XII", "U",
+    "S", "C", "F", "G", "WARN", "SUMF", "LOI", "HR",
+    "A", "B", "D", "E", "H", "J", "K", "L", "M", "N", "O", "P", "Q", "R",
+    "T", "V", "W", "Y", "Z",
+    "Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Sept", "Oct",
+    "Nov", "Dec",
+    "Mr", "Mrs", "Ms", "Dr", "Prof", "Hon", "Rev", "Re", "Vs", "Et", "Al",
+    "Act", "Tab", "Tabs", "Workbook", "Note", "Notes",
+    "First", "Second", "Third", "Fourth", "Fifth", "Sixth", "Seventh",
+    "Eighth", "Ninth", "Tenth",
+}
+TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9'’]*|&|[.!?]")
+ROMAN_RE = re.compile(r"^[IVXLC]+$")
+UPPER_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Z]{3,}$")
+ALLOW_UPPER = {"WARN", "SUMF", "LOI", "HR"}
+
+
+def read(path):
+    try:
+        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
+            return f.read().replace("’", "'")
+    except OSError as e:
+        print(f"ERROR: cannot read {path}: {e}")
+        sys.exit(2)
+
+
+def is_breaker(tok):
+    if tok in BREAKERS or tok == "&":
+        return False
+    if tok in ALLOW_UPPER:
+        return True
+    if UPPER_RE.match(tok) or ROMAN_RE.match(tok) and len(tok) > 1:
+        return True
+    return False
+
+
+def entities(text):
+    tokens = TOKEN_RE.findall(text)
+    tokens = [t[:-2] if t.endswith("'s") else t for t in tokens]
+    raw = []
+    run = []
+
+    def emit():
+        ws = [w for w in run if w != "&"]
+        if 2 <= len(run) <= 4 and len(set(ws)) == len(ws):
+            raw.append(" ".join(run))
+
+    for tok in tokens + ["|"]:
+        if tok == "&":
+            run.append(tok)
+        elif tok in BREAKERS or is_breaker(tok) or tok in ".!?":
+            emit()
+            run = []
+        elif re.match(r"^[A-Z]", tok):
+            run.append(tok)
+        else:
+            emit()
+            run = []
+    return Counter(raw)
+
+
+def words(entity):
+    return set(w for w in entity.split() if w != "&")
+
+
+def singular(w):
+    return w[:-1] if len(w) > 3 and w.endswith("s") else w
+
+
+def exact_related(d, s):
+    if d == s:
+        return True
+    dws, sws = words(d), words(s)
+    if dws == sws:
+        return True
+    if {singular(w) for w in dws} == {singular(w) for w in sws}:
+        return "plural"
+    return False
+
+
+def score(d, s):
+    dws, sws = words(d), words(s)
+    inter = len(dws & sws)
+    union = len(dws | sws)
+    j = inter / union if union else 0.0
+    dtok, stok = d.split(), s.split()
+    bonus = 0.2 if (dtok[0] == stok[0] or dtok[-1] == stok[-1]) else 0.0
+    return j + bonus
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--deliverable", required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--sources", nargs="+", required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--min-freq", type=int, default=2,
+                    help="minimum deliverable repetitions for the UNSUPPORTED list")
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+
+    src_text = "\n".join(read(p) for p in args.sources)
+    del_text = read(args.deliverable)
+    src_ents = entities(src_text)
+    del_ents = entities(del_text)
+
+    print(f"sources: {len(args.sources)} file(s), {len(src_ents)} distinct names")
+    print(f"deliverable: {args.deliverable}, {len(del_ents)} distinct names\n")
+
+    src_by_word = {}
+    for e in src_ents:
+        for w in words(e):
+            src_by_word.setdefault(w, set()).add(e)
+
+    plural_hits, mutated, unsupported = [], [], []
+    for d in sorted(del_ents):
+        cands = set()
+        for w in words(d):
+            cands |= src_by_word.get(w, set())
+        rel = None
+        best, best_s = None, 0.0
+        for s in cands:
+            r = exact_related(d, s)
+            if r is True:
+                rel = s
+                break
+            sc = score(d, s)
+            if r == "plural":
+                sc += 1.0
+            if sc > best_s:
+                best, best_s = s, sc
+        if rel is not None:
+            continue
+        if best is not None and best_s >= 1.0:
+            plural_hits.append((d, best, del_ents[d]))
+        elif best is not None and best_s >= 0.45:
+            mutated.append((d, best, del_ents[d]))
+        elif del_ents[d] >= args.min_freq:
+            unsupported.append((d, del_ents[d]))
+
+    for title, rows in (("PLURAL DRIFT — same name, different form:", plural_hits),
+                        ("MUTATED — deliverable name resembles a DIFFERENT source name:",
+                         mutated)):
+        print(title)
+        if rows:
+            for d, s, n in rows:
+                print(f"  deliverable {d!r} (x{n})  <-- source has  {s!r}")
+        else:
+            print("  none")
+        print()
+    print(f"UNSUPPORTED — repeated in the deliverable, no counterpart in any source "
+          f"(freq >= {args.min_freq}):")
+    if unsupported:
+        for d, n in unsupported:
+            print(f"  {d!r} (x{n})")
+    else:
+        print("  none")
+    print("\nCheck every PLURAL DRIFT and MUTATED line against the record before "
+          "release; UNSUPPORTED lines are acceptable only if coined deliberately.")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# Tool Guidance
+
+Verified facts about the workspace tools. Follow these instead of
+rediscovering them by trial and error.
+
+## Document extraction sandbox
+
+`scripts/read_doc.py` runs its converter inside a sandbox that defaults to
+a container runtime. On this machine the runtime is not installed, and the
+default invocation fails with `FileNotFoundError` naming the container
+binary. Always pass host input mode:
+
+    python3 scripts/read_doc.py <document.docx> --in host
+
+If a command fails twice the same way, stop repeating it and read its
+`--help`.
+
+## Where scratch files may live
+
+The sandbox `external_directory` rule blocks reading and writing outside
+the workspace, including `/tmp`. Run scripts from the workspace root and
+keep scratch inputs and outputs (extracted text, throwaway verification
+scripts) in workspace-relative paths.
+
+## Truncated command output
+
+Tool output above roughly 50 KB is truncated in the transcript, and the
+full output is saved to a file whose path is printed in the truncation
+notice, under `.ocdata/opencode/tool-output/`. Do not re-run an expensive
+extraction to see content you already produced: read or grep that saved
+file instead. This matters most after context compaction — re-reading
+whole documents you already extracted wastes large amounts of context;
+grep the saved extractions.
+
+## Spreadsheet inspection
